emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(m->err)]) from thread_b (the lockless error check must be a single-copy read, not torn by the cancel write)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@p9_conn_cancel:200 = WRITE(m->err = err) by thread_a under m->req_lock
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: thread_a writes under m->req_lock, but thread_b reads m->err WITHOUT taking req_lock (deliberate fast-path to skip work after an error) -> no common lock serializes the read against the write
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic(single access) broken by a (lock-protected) write racing a lockless read -> data race; canonical 'lock-protected write + lockless read', explicitly benign

fix_maps_to: patch marks the write WRITE_ONCE (+ASSERT_EXCLUSIVE_WRITER) and the lockless reads READ_ONCE -> single-copy atomicity for the lockless reads; req_lock stays only on the write side, NO new exclusion/order for the read -> maps to atomic([read]) at the access-marking level only
recall_risk_notes: Benign by design (commit message id literally 'benign_data_race'): the lockless read is an intentional fast-path; the value is re-checked under lock where it matters. required_ordering = 'mark the lockless reads'. The arbiter would likely reject the atomic(read) assume as a real requirement -> FN, or fire only a low-value syntactic-race finding. Structurally clean (writer holds req_lock, reader does not), so IF the design fires on lock-protected-write/lockless-read shapes it would match.
